title: Vibe — Publication Pack 1
description: Intent-first language and local-first compiler architecture with preservation-gated emission, public proof boundaries, and a fixed-data Intent Preservation Workbench.

projects.title: Vibe
projects.tagline: A local-first intent-first language and compiler where preservation obligations gate whether generated artifacts may be emitted.
projects.story: Vibe makes human intent the source object rather than a disposable prompt. A .vibe specification is parsed and lowered into typed intermediate representation, converted into preservation and constraint obligations, evaluated by configured verifier backends, and reported through machine-checkable proof metadata. Emission occurs only when the implemented bridge and preservation gate passes.
projects.summary: A working prototype compiler and toolchain with bounded language and domain slices, deterministic-by-default local workflows, proof artifacts, snapshots, package and registry operations, LSP and CI surfaces, semantic intent diff, versioning, negotiation, interchange artifacts, standard-library intent contracts, and PhiPython as a guided Python layer inside Vibe.
projects.see: The Vibe cover, compiler pipeline, preservation gate, architecture and command-boundary briefs, fixed-data Intent Preservation Workbench, PAT Compiler Mode, verified public repository, canonical payment-router example, and planned command-atlas and safe-mode artifacts.
projects.proof: Eight public artifacts are connected. The Workbench deterministically evaluates six bundled synthetic intent fixtures and produces non-canonical proof/report previews while accepting no visitor source, invoking no real compiler, executing no code, applying no patch, making no network or model call, persisting no state, and emitting no production target.
projects.next: Publish VIBE_COMMAND_ATLAS.md and the safe-mode policy in the Vibe repository, freeze a public deterministic fixture and proof bundle, then connect SIGLStudio as a consumer of Vibe’s canonical intent and proof surfaces without duplicating the verification logic.
projects.claimBoundary: Vibe is a working prototype compiler with implemented bounded language and domain slices. This package demonstrates public architecture and deterministic teaching fixtures; it does not establish complete language coverage, universal intent understanding, full formal verification of arbitrary program semantics, complete theorem proving, guaranteed correctness, safety certification, legal approval, deployment authority, human authorization, preservation of unstated expectations, or permission to modify code, data, systems, money, accounts, contracts, or people. Current Vibe proof means machine-checkable metadata produced by the implemented verifier and proof pipeline. PhiPython explanations, doctor checks, generated tests, candidate fixes, repair receipts, and review bundles remain bounded guidance and local review artifacts rather than formal correctness proofs.

relationships.note: ALO preserves source identity, verifier results, emission decisions, patch review, exceptions, rollback, and repair continuity.
SOSA can govern who may approve intent changes, accept proof boundaries, authorize emission, operate targets, dissent, and repair failures.

relationships.type: structured intent contracts for computational collaboration
relationships.note: Agentora can consume Vibe contracts so multiple Computational Collaborators work from explicit goals, constraints, authorities, and proof surfaces.
SignalBridge can package Vibe intent and proof briefs into bounded handoff candidates without converting preservation into production authority.
Census tracks Vibe releases, examples, proof fixtures, policy artifacts, aliases, custody, and public publication states.
Double C clarifies that Vibe structures human-led collaboration with Computational Collaborators rather than replacing human intent or authority.
Archive Core presents the compiler architecture and fixed teaching fixtures while linking to the verified public source repository.
